catalog_locator: Doke 1936: p. 433, opening paragraph, and section 'Tone', pp. 440-441 (pp. 1 and 8-9 of the extract = pp. 69 and 76-77 of the archive.org whole-issue scan). Exter 2008: §3.4, pp. 54-55.
catalog_quote: The phonetics of this section of the Southern Bushmen closely resembles in general features that of the ˈǃkhũ, a tribe of Northern Bushmen, whom I studied in 1925. The basis of most words is monosyllabic, tone occurs but not stress, and the range of tones seems to be the same as with ˈǃkhũ. As with ˈǃkhũ, so with ǂkhomani all syllables end with vowels or nasal consonants. [...] Tone, the musical modulation of the voice in speech, is a most important feature of ǂkhomani as of other Bushman languages. Many words alike in phonetic make-up, but bearing different meanings, are only distinguishable tonetically. [...] As in the case of ˈǃkhũ, so in ǂkhomani, I found five species of tone, though the rising and falling tones were more rarely used. The five tones are (i) High-level (¯a), (ii) Mid-level (a), (iii) Low-level (_a), (iv) rising (ˊa) and (v) falling (ˋa). The diacritics are placed immediately at the commencement of the syllable indicated, no diacritic being used for the mid-level tone. The tones do not indicate an actual but a relative pitch. (Doke 1936: 433, 440) [Corroboration, Exter 2008: 54-55: 'A preliminary investigation of the data available to me has shown that there seem to be two underlying lexical tones, high (H) and low (L). [...] Like in ǃXóõ (Naumann 2008, pace Traill 1977), The mora is the tone bearing unit in Nǀuu']
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: While it has been acknowledged before by Miller et al. (2007, 2009) that Nǀuu is indeed a tone language (like all other 'Khoisan' languages), the tonal structure of the language has not been described in detail so far. A preliminary investigation of the data available to me has shown that there seem to be two underlying lexical tones, high (H) and low (L). [...] Like in ǃXóõ (Naumann 2008, pace Traill 1977), The mora is the tone bearing unit in Nǀuu; this means that within any given syllable, each nuclear element (i.e. vowel or syllabic nasal) and each coda element (i.e. syllable-final nasal, if present) bears exactly one tone.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again: Exter 2008. opened (156 pp., KUPS Koeln, URL re-verified HTTP 200 application/pdf 3530032 bytes). Section 3.4 'Lexical Tones' begins on printed p. 54 = p. 61 and runs to p. 56; the quoted passage is there verbatim (first sentence and 'there seem to be two underlying lexical tones, high (H) and low (L)' on p. 54; 'Like in !Xoo (Naumann 2008, pace Traill 1977), The mora is the tone bearing unit in Nuu.. bears exactly one tone.' on p. 55, capital 'The' as in the source; the [..] elides the transcription sentence and example (3.27)). Section 4.1 'The Prosodic Structure' pp. 57-61 (pp. 64-68) gives the foot template (4.1) and root types (4.4); the 'strongest pros…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Nǀuu is a two-tone (H/L) language with the mora as tone-bearing unit; lexical roots consist of one to three feet (1-4 morae), with an obligatory 'core' foot whose initial position C1 is called the strongest prosodic position (it hosts the clicks). The source makes no statement about word stress or accent at all; nothing in the opened material assigns stress to a position.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone: three reduplicated items and two ideophones excluded from the tonal statistics (p. 71); surface LH realized as mid level between H and a low boundary tone (rule 3.28, p. 56). Nothing on stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical roots/phonological words elicited in the frame 'ná ká __' (I say __); Exter explicitly says larger prosodic units and intonation are unstudied (fn. 20, p. 57; p. 145). Data are the author's own fieldwork on Nǀuu (Western dialect speakers of the ǂKhomani community, Upington area).
new_statements.identity_note: Exter 2008 describes Nǀuu as spoken by the ǂKhomani community elders near Upington (Western variety, Namaseb/Collins/Miller/Sands project); Doke 1936 and Maingard 1937 describe ǂKhomani (Eastern lect); Bleek/Güldemann 2000 describe ǁŋ!ke of Griqualand West. All are lects of nngg1234 (Nǁng; ISO ngh); no separate glottocodes.

tone.quote: Tone is not marked in the N uu orthography, even though there is evidence that lexical tone is in fact a distinctive feature in N uu (Exter 2008). Exter (2015) provides minimal pairs for this ‘ for example, / / ‘blanket’ versus / / ‘house’. Since Ouma Geelmeid does not consistently produce such tonal differences, tone is not marked in the N uu orthography.
